quotes.text: Build a simpler mobile integration with regional limitations.

old_evidence.text: This integration supports businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards.
Always decide how much to charge on the server, a trusted environment, as opposed to the client.
If the payment was successful, it will have a status of `succeeded`.

findings: The complete November 2026 capture retains the title and regional-limitation description and lists iOS, Android and React Native variant links without their bodies (new raw 1–15; old raw 4–12, 335–340 and 630–635). The old capture was fetched 2026-04-23 despite the filename. Diff line 931 joins the old ending and first new link, and the actual snapshots give the boundary (old raw 926–930; new raw 13–15).

The 2026-04-23 restricted integration is for businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards. Client card fields collect sensitive details and `createPaymentMethod` supplies an ID to the merchant server. The server decides the amount and creates/confirms a PaymentIntent with `confirm: true` and `error_on_requires_action: true`. The immediate server result supports post-payment actions when `succeeded`; an authentication request causes an error rather than customer authentication (old raw 12–34, 112–178, 180–265, 290–316, 414–473 and 715–775).

The existing source correctly retains the basic approach and three separate platform UI components. Its use criterion weakens the old card scope, its webhook language omits the restriction to immediate actions in the synchronous server flow, and its response prose obscures non-authentication card declines and unexpected server outcomes. A correct retrieval answer also needs the explicit server-owned amount and the distinction between creating the client PaymentMethod and server payment success (source 13–34, 38–58; old raw 12–34, 162–178, 191–196 and 216–325).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the 2026-04-23 scope to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards and preserve the tradeoff that an issuer request for authentication causes a decline instead of an authentication flow. The April guide routes growing/global businesses and authentication-required payments toward Stripe’s authentication-capable integration (old raw 12–34 and 329–333, repeated for Android and React Native).

Keep the dated iOS `STPPaymentCardTextField` in `StripePaymentsUI`, Android `CardInputWidget`, and React Native `CardField`, with client-side card collection and PaymentMethod creation followed by passing its ID to a trusted server. The examples use publishable client configuration and distinguish test keys from live keys. Android 23.5.0 and iOS 13 are historic sample claims. The Financial Connections dependency comment concerns US bank accounts, while this payment guide describes cards (old raw 38–48, 93–114, 162–195, 369–414, 454–490, 682–719 and 754–792).

Preserve the server-authoritative amount and immediate confirm attempt. The sample uses `succeeded` to gate immediate fulfillment and treats other returned statuses as unexpected. The authentication failure example shows `authentication_required`, `authentication_not_handled` and `requires_payment_method`; the insufficient-funds and successful cards are separate test scenarios (old raw 191–265 and 290–327).

The archived explanation permits immediate post-payment actions from the synchronous server result in this restricted path. The comparison table recommends webhooks in the global integration (old raw 18–34). PaymentMethod creation, a success-path API example, and sandbox test outcomes do not establish live payment, settlement, broad eligibility, or current SDK support.
conflicts: Source line 17 says `primarily accepts US/Canada cards`, although the old guide’s scope says businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards (old raw 12, 339 and 634). The related index/concept descriptions should keep the restriction attached to card scope instead of making it a claim about merchant account geography.

Source lines 13, 48 and 57 and reciprocal in-app concept line 113 compress the restricted synchronous example into a general no-webhook claim. Old raw 18–34 and 245–255 scope that to immediate post-payment actions from the server’s `succeeded` branch, and the global route recommends webhooks.

Source lines 34 and 48 can make `authentication_required`/`authentication_not_handled` look like the only error alternative. The specific API example has those codes and `requires_payment_method`, while the server sample has a separate unexpected-status and non-card-error path and the test table has insufficient funds (old raw 234–255, 290–325). The React Native initialization comment about a 3D Secure return URL is generic and does not override the restricted flow’s deliberate refusal to handle the issuer request (old raw 634–656, 701–706 and 823–857).
unresolved_questions: The linked November variant bodies are outside the capture. Current SDK, OS and API compatibility, account eligibility and live outcomes remain unverified.

findings: Preserve the April detailed capture and add the November navigation reference, date the historical API/UI and test examples, and maintain the reciprocal in-app concept route (source 6–8 and 72–78; old raw 1–12; new raw 1–15).

Correct the explicit use criterion in source 17 to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards. Reinforce that this route uses client-side card collection and a PaymentMethod ID, with the server deciding the amount and creating/confirming a distinct PaymentIntent (source 13–34 and 44–48; old raw 12–34, 162–195 and 216–232).

Replace broad no-webhook and response shorthand with the dated server-authoritative `succeeded` fulfillment branch, the separate authentication-error example and unexpected/card-error paths, and the global authentication-capable route (source 13, 18, 34, 48, 57 and 70; old raw 18–34, 234–265 and 290–333).
conflicts: Source 17 says `primarily` and its own line 13 says `only`. The April raw repeats `only` at 12, 339 and 634.

Source 13, 48 and 57 and in-app concept 113 risk applying no-webhook language outside this immediate server response. Source 34 also treats sample authentication errors as a general response category (old raw 18–34, 234–265 and 290–325).
source_assessments.reason: The new raw is navigation only. The baseline source needs correction because its use criterion can select the regional flow for unsupported card populations, and its outcome shorthand can obscure the trusted success condition and correct error interpretation.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/without-card-authentication, new raw lines 5-15 describe a simpler region-limited integration and route to iOS, Android and React Native. The April 23, 2026 capture supplies the actual behavior. Old raw lines 12-34 scope it to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards and say an issuer authentication request immediately fails the payment. Old raw lines 112-178, 414-473 and 715-775 show the separate client card fields and creation of a PaymentMethod whose ID goes to the server. The server chooses the amount and creates and confirms a PaymentIntent with `confirm: true` and `error_on_requires_action: true`. The sample gates immediate fulfillment on server-observed `succeeded`, while the authentication-error example uses `authentication_required`, `authentication_not_handled` and `requires_payment_method` (old raw lines 191-265 and 290-316). source-stripe-inapp-without-card-auth.md captures the core path but needs to correct its looser regional use criterion and scope its no-webhook and error wording to the documented example.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/without-card-authentication, new raw lines 5-15 add only navigation to the platform variants represented in old raw lines 8-12, 335-340 and 630-635. The pinned evidence shows no substantive product change. Date the April 23, 2026 scope to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards and distinguish the client PaymentMethod from the server-created and immediately confirmed PaymentIntent. The April example applies its no-webhook shortcut only to immediate post-payment actions from the trusted server response, with fulfillment gated on `succeeded`. The global route handles authentication requests and recommends webhooks (old raw lines 12-34 and 193-265). In source-stripe-inapp-without-card-auth.md and the reciprocal in-app route, qualify the regional criterion and no-webhook wording, keep issuer-authentication errors separate from insufficient-funds and other errors, and retain the platform UI and sandbox distinctions (old raw lines 112-178, 290-333, 414-473 and 715-775). A test response or the new index cannot verify current compatibility, merchant eligibility, live payment success or settlement.
